catalogue_requests.reason: no catalogue class switches a power-supply output off as a no-input safe-state action; cap.device.configure.v1 is a write class whose binding needs a field value and cannot serve @action(safe_state=True), so the package uses an x-cap id with an inline output schema for OUTP CHn,OFF on both channels
catalogue_requests.summary: Disable both channel outputs of the Siglent SPD3303 series (OUTP CH1,OFF and OUTP CH2,OFF); the declared safe state.

notes:
Passed the acceptance gate on the fake backend with all nine gates passing and no findings or warnings (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). No hardware was attached; native.py was never imported or run and there is no hardware-run claim. This package is model-authored (driver.lock.json authored_by kind model) and unreviewed (reviewed_by null). It is R1, so the loader does not refuse its hardware backend: nothing mechanical prevents a hardware run, and a human must review the package before anyone passes --allow-hardware. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names helper PythonObjectDriver; the package is a decorated direct Driver over instro.psu.drivers.siglent_spd3303:SiglentSPD3303, because each device operation is one typed method on the upstream class and the class owns its own VISA transport. The card decision direct-driver is unchanged and no wire syntax was changed. The driver covers channels 1 and 2 only: the upstream SCPI class treats channel 3 as front-panel selectable without a programming interface (instro/psu/drivers/siglent_spd3303.py:189-197). Reads are the two voltage and current set points, the measured voltage and current, the output-enable state, the regulation mode and the tracking mode. Writes are the four numeric set points and the two output-enable booleans through cap.device.configure.v1. Every numeric set point is Limit.operator_required because the clone states no numeric output range for the SPD3303 series; site-limits.example.json is an example overlay only (0-30 V and 0-3 A) and is not a statement about any unit, so until an operator supplies the installed unit's range each of those writes is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. The candidate classes cap.measure.voltage.v1 and cap.measure.current.v1 were not bound: their resource kinds are instrument.dmm, instrument.smu and sensor, while this DC source declares kind instrument; measured values are served as read state and cap.device.configure.v1 serves the writes. cap.actuation.gpio.v1 does not fit a power supply. The safe-state action x-cap.nominal-io.output_off.v1 and the @estop both call the native output_enable(False, channel) on both channels. The clone documents no independent hardware e-stop, so estop_physical_ref is not set and no hardware stop is claimed; the software latch and the safe-state action are not a safety-rated channel. Mock path: the card preferred the upstream PSU simulator, but instro/psu/scpi_sim_server.py is a TCP SCPI server (line 698-721), the clone may not be imported or run, and the gate runs with no network; fake.py is therefore an in-memory stand-in with exactly the public method shapes of the upstream class, and every starting value, measured value and status string in it is a placeholder, not a recording. The fake models a resistive load only to make a measurement move with the set points; it is not a calibration. The device is scalar only, so there is no array to leave uncovered. No PDF page is cited and there are no G4 REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest the passing check printed.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-30; reviewed_by stays null): accepted; the reviewer changed no file of the package. After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.
